The fact that PTP 2-step TX timestamping is broken on DSA switches if
the master also timestamps the same packets is documented by commit
f685e609a301 (""net: dsa: Deny PTP on master if switch supports it"").
We attempt to help the users avoid shooting themselves in the foot by
making DSA reject the timestamping ioctls on an interface that is a DSA
master
column2: and the switch tree beneath it contains switches which are aware

column1: of PTP.
The only problem is that there isn't an established way of intercepting
ndo_eth_ioctl calls
column2: so DSA creates avoidable burden upon the network

column1: stack by creating a struct dsa_netdevice_ops with overlaid function
pointers that are manually checked from the relevant call sites. There
used to be 2 such dsa_netdevice_ops
column2: but now

column1: one left.
There is an ongoing effort to migrate driver-visible hardware timestamping
control from the ndo_eth_ioctl() based API to a new ndo_hwtstamp_set()
model
column2: but DSA actively prevents that migration

column1: is currently coded to manually call the master's legacy ndo_eth_ioctl()
and so
column2: whenever a network device driver would be converted to the new

column1: API
column2: DSA's restrictions would be circumvented

column1: be used as a DSA master.
The established way for unrelated modules to react on a net device event
is via netdevice notifiers. So we create a new notifier which gets
called whenever there is an attempt to change hardware timestamping
settings on a device.
Finally
column2: there is another reason why a netdev notifier will be a good

column1: idea
column2: besides strictly DSA
column3: and this has to do with PHY timestamping.

column1: With ndo_eth_ioctl()
column2: all MAC drivers must manually call

column1: phy_has_hwtstamp() before deciding whether to act upon SIOCSHWTSTAMP
otherwise they must pass this ioctl to the PHY driver via
phy_mii_ioctl().
With the new ndo_hwtstamp_set() API
column2: it will be desirable to simply not

column1: make any calls into the MAC device driver when timestamping should be
performed at the PHY level.
But there exist drivers
column2: such as the lan966x switch

column1: install packet traps for PTP regardless of whether they are the layer
that provides the hardware timestamps
column2: or the PHY is. That would be

column1: impossible to support with the new API.
The proposal there
column2: too
column3: is to introduce a netdev notifier which acts as

column1: a better cue for switching drivers to add or remove PTP packet traps
than ndo_hwtstamp_set(). The one introduced here ""almost"" works there as
well
column2: except for the fact that packet traps should only be installed if

column1: the PHY driver succeeded to enable hardware timestamping
column2: whereas here

column1: we need to deny hardware timestamping on the DSA master before it
actually gets enabled. This is why this notifier is called ""PRE_""
column2: and

column1: the notifier that would get used for PHY timestamping and packet traps
would be called NETDEV_CHANGE_HWTSTAMP. This isn't a new concept
column2: for

column1: example NETDEV_CHANGEUPPER and NETDEV_PRECHANGEUPPER do the same thing.
In expectation of future netlink UAPI
column2: we also pass a non-NULL extack

column1: pointer to the netdev notifier
column2: and we make DSA populate it with an

column1: informative reason for the rejection. To avoid making it go to waste
column2: we

column1: make the ioctl-based dev_set_hwtstamp() create a fake extack and print
the message to the kernel log.
